question: Which of the following satellites is India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Astrosat.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Astrosat:**

 
 
• **It is India’s first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory.**
 
• This scientific satellite mission was launched on** September 28, 2015,** and endeavours for a more detailed understanding of our universe.
 
• Its objective was to study celestial sources in **X-ray, optical, and UV spectral bands** as it will help in the better understanding of the universe.
 
• **It has a mission life of 5 years.**
 
• Its successful launch made India members of the select elite group of nations comprising the** US, Japan, Russia, and Europe** have their own space observatory.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
**SRMSat**

 
 
 
By the students and faculty of SRM University

 
 
 
 
• The nanosatellite SRMSat weighing 10.9 kg is developed to attempt to address the problem of Global warming and pollution levels in the atmosphere by monitoring Carbon dioxide (CO2) and water vapor (H2O).
 
 
 
 

 
 
**SARAL**

 
 
 
ISRO

 
 
 
 
• The Satellite with ARGOS and ALTIKA (SARAL) is a joint Indo-French satellite, designed for oceanographic studies.
 
• SARAL performs altimetric measurements designed to study ocean circulation and sea surface elevation.
 
 
 
 

 
 
**JUGNU**

 
 
 
IIT, Kanpur

 
 
 
 
• To prove the indigenously developed camera system for imaging the Earth in the near-infrared region and test image processing algorithms.
